summary: dotenv-precheck postinstall harvests wallet seeds, private keys, and.env secrets to Telegram bot
details: dotenv-precheck 1.1.0 ships a single heavily obfuscated index.js (obfuscator.io-style string-array indirection, self-defense wrapper, base64-decoded constants, embedded ~13KB base64 BIP-39 wordlist, _0xNNNN variable mangling) that is registered as a postinstall lifecycle script. On npm install it recursively walks directories above the install location and the user's home, Desktop, Documents, and Downloads, reads.env and other text files, and extracts wallet mnemonics (BIP-39 wordlist match), 0x-prefixed 64-char hex private keys, WIF keys, Solana 64-integer arrays, and any environment variable whose name matches KEY/SECRET/TOKEN/PASSWORD/SEED/MNEMONIC/WALLET/CREDENTIAL. The collected JSON payload (env files, private keys, seed phrases) is exfiltrated via fetch to a base64-hidden api.telegram.org sendMessage and sendDocument endpoint using a hardcoded bot token and chat id. The package name and 'dotenv preflight checks' description are a cover story; no preflight functionality is implemented. This is a supply-chain credential and crypto-wallet stealer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
